text: Git branching is a key part of the version control workflow. When you start working on a new feature, you create a feature branch, which lets you make changes without affecting the main code. Once your work is finished, you merge the branch back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often use pull requests. A pull request lets other developers review your changes, discuss them, and suggest improvements. This process helps catch mistakes early and keeps the code clean. By using feature branches, merging, and pull requests together, teams can work on different tasks at the same time and keep their projects organised and safe.
